body: ENFP and ENTP share E, N and P; their codes differ on F/T. Feeling emphasizes values and effects on people in decisions, while Thinking emphasizes logical consistency and impersonal criteria. This is not an emotional-versus-rational ability ranking.
sections.title: quick_answer

body: Both codes describe Extraversion, Intuition and Perceiving: attention toward the outer world, patterns or possibilities, and openness to incoming information. In type narratives, both may explore alternatives through discussion. They need not have the same social energy, imagination or interests.

The difference is how a decision is considered. An ENFP-style question might ask whether an idea serves a value and the people involved; an ENTP-style question might ask whether its explanation and criteria hold together. Both can consider values and logic. The distinction concerns preference, not access to either process.

Function-stack theory commonly uses Ne–Fi–Te–Si for ENFP and Ne–Ti–Fe–Si for ENTP. This is a theoretical convention, not proof of distinct mental mechanisms or a shortcut to typing someone. A/T is a separate extension and does not resolve the F/T distinction.
sections.title: What is shared and what differs

body:
| Observation | ENFP | ENTP |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code difference | Feeling (F): values and effects on people | Thinking (T): logical consistency and impersonal criteria |
| Original funding example | Check whether a proposal preserves the stated purpose | Check whether the selection rule is consistent |
| Possible blind spot | Assuming a valued purpose is enough to justify the implementation | Assuming a consistent rule includes every relevant human consequence |
| Shared practical step | Explain the value and test the actual effect | Explain the rule and examine whose needs it omits |
sections.title: Side-by-side comparison

body: Original work scenario: a team must choose which community project receives a limited grant. One approach examines who is served and whether the proposal fits the mission; another checks whether the selection criteria can be applied consistently. Combine both: state the purpose, apply the criteria and inspect the consequences. The same person can contribute both approaches.

Original relationship scenario: two friends disagree over cancelling a plan. One focuses on the meaning of the commitment; another compares the stated reasons and whether the rule would apply next time. Ask about the practical need and the value at stake. Do not interpret a focus on criteria as lack of care or a focus on feelings as poor reasoning.
sections.title: Examples in work and relationships

body: Enjoying debate does not identify ENTP, and being warm does not identify ENFP. F does not mean emotional instability, and T does not mean emotional absence. Both can reason rigorously, care deeply, follow routines and finish work. Do not use humor, career interests or how often someone cries as a typing rule.
sections.title: Avoid these misreadings

body: Compare three decisions with genuine tradeoffs. What criterion did you consult first, what did you find difficult to set aside and what could change your mind? Include a counterexample where you preferred the other approach. Check whether your role required a particular criterion. If both descriptions fit, leave the question open rather than treating a narrative match as a verified result.
sections.title: How to continue your self-observation

body: The official MBTI describes four preference pairs. A/T belongs to a separate extension; shared letters do not make different tests equivalent. Type narratives and cognitive functions are theoretical interpretations, not established psychological mechanisms.

McCrae and Costa (1989) compared the 1985 MBTI with NEO-PI self-reports and peer ratings in 267 men and 201 women aged 19–93; the abstract does not identify a representative country sample. Their analysis did not support true dichotomies or qualitatively distinct types and found overlap with dimensions of the five-factor model. Instrument editions and samples matter: the publisher reports later revisions, and this page does not establish the reliability or validity of a FermatMind score. That specific study does not validate these scenarios, determine an individual's type or settle every question about later instruments.

A newer review by Erford and colleagues (2025) synthesized 193 studies using English-language MBTI Form M, published during 1999–2024. It reported favorable internal-consistency estimates (0.845–0.921) and convergent evidence, while finding no independent structural-validity or test–retest studies in its eligible literature beyond the manual. Score consistency does not establish distinct natural types, validate A/T, or transfer to FermatMind. Both supportive findings and remaining gaps depend on the specific instrument and samples.

The situations and exercises on this page are original educational examples, not clinical guidance or findings about groups. Compare them with your experience, including counterexamples. Do not use type alone to diagnose, hire, choose a career or screen a relationship.
